title: Joints, Camera, Action! Co-Generating 3D Motion and Video for Arbitrary Rigs
why_read: A technically interesting approach to jointly generating video and 3D motion for arbitrary skeletons, relevant to graphics and animation researchers.
analysis: This paper tackles turning AI-generated video into usable 3D animation data for arbitrary character rigs, not just humans, by co-generating video and motion through a model that cross-attends to a pretrained video generator. The key technical contribution is separating a flexible motion model from the video model so it can learn from motion-only data, which is cheaper to collect than paired video. It also recovers camera placement so the generated motion fits back into a 3D scene, enabling practical workflows like keyframe-based control. This is a solid systems-level advance for animators and game/VFX pipelines rather than a fundamental breakthrough.
